extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/agents, patent drafters, and patent prosecution teams (US practice)
extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step practitioner workflow for drafting a patent application from initial inventor disclosure through filing and immediate post‑filing calendaring, with phase-by-phase outputs and checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 - Invention Capture (Days 1-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce an invention disclosure by sitting with the inventor, walking through the invention from problem to solution, taking notes and sketching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The output disclosure should include: Problem statement (technical, not commercial); Closest known prior solutions and their shortcomings; The new solution explained step by step; Alternative implementations and variations; Any test data or performance results. (Timing: Days 1-3.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 - Prior Art Search (Days 3-10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a professional search of patents and non-patent literature in the relevant field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report should identify the 5-10 closest references with detailed analysis of which claim elements each one discloses. (Timing: Days 3-10.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 3 - Claim Strategy (Days 10-12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide overall claim strategy based on the search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should address: what is the broadest claim scope that distinguishes over the closest art; the key narrowing dimensions for dependent claims; what claim types (method, system, apparatus, CRM) make sense; and the overall portfolio architecture (single filing vs. a family of filings). (Timing: Days 10-12.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 4 - Independent Claim Drafting (Days 12-15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft multiple independent claims of varying scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft 3-4 independent claims. The broadest is the 'moonshot'; the narrowest is the 'picture claim'. Cross-check each independent claim against the closest art to confirm distinguishing elements. (Timing: Days 12-15.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 5 - Dependent Claims (Days 15-18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a ladder of dependent claims that narrow the independent claims across different dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a claim ladder that systematically narrows on different dimensions. Each rung should be independently meaningful and not a trivial restatement. (Timing: Days 15-18.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 6 - Specification Drafting (Days 18-30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft the specification by describing figures, interactions, alternatives, and ensuring support for claim terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Walk through the figures one at a time; describe what each shows, how the components interact, and what alternatives exist. Ensure every claim term has antecedent support in the spec. Include 'in some embodiments' framings throughout. (Timing: Days 18-30.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 7 - Drawings (Days 25-30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce formal patent drawings from engineering sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage a patent draftsperson to convert engineering sketches into formal patent drawings (37 CFR 1.84 compliant). Ensure each reference number in the spec appears in at least one figure. (Timing: Days 25-30.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 8 - Inventor review for technical accuracy (Days 30-35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the inventor review the draft for technical correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor should confirm that the disclosure, figures, embodiments, and examples accurately reflect the invention and any test data. (Timing: Days 30-35.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 8 - Senior attorney review for legal sufficiency (Days 30-35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a senior attorney review the draft for legal sufficiency and prosecution robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior attorney should check claim scope, support in the spec, prosecution strategy, and litigation considerations. (Timing: Days 30-35.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify antecedent basis for claim terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run through checklist to ensure every claim term has proper antecedent support in the specification and consistent introduction/definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistent terminology across claims and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the same term is used consistently and synonyms are avoided where they would create ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — claim ladder
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the claim ladder is systematic and meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check dependent claims form a logical ladder that narrows across different dimensions rather than repeating the same limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — embodiment count
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess number and variety of embodiments disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure multiple embodiments and variations are described to support broad claim scope and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — no patent profanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or avoid 'patent profanity' in the specification or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure language that could unduly limit claim scope or introduce admissions (so-called 'patent profanity') is identified and corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist — IDS prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm identified prior art and search results are documented and an IDS is ready to be submitted with the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 9 - Filing (Day 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: File the application electronically and submit required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File electronically through Patent Center. Submit specification, claims, abstract, drawings, oath/declaration, application data sheet, and IDS. Pay filing fees. (Timing: Day 35.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 10 - Post-Filing Calendar
rubrics_metrics.description: Calendar key post-filing deadlines and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include 12-month foreign filing deadline, 18-month publication, expected first office action date, and deadlines for any continuations to be filed before parent issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Checks Throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing evaluative questions to apply at every phase of the workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each phase, ask: does this still distinguish over the closest art? does the spec still support the claims? would I be comfortable with this in litigation? does this leave room for design-around?
